title: 🥖 Darden variety
body_text: Join us this morning in raising a cup of ambition to celebrate the inaugural “Dolly Parton Day.” The 25th of September (9/25) ((nine-two-five, for those already mentally checked out for the weekend)) has been officially recognized to commemorate the star by the state of California, cities from Nashville to Manhattan, and various counties across the US. Naturally, participants are encouraged to honor Dolly by spreading kindness, wearing pink, and listening to “9 to 5” at 5 p.m. local time, wherever they are celebrating. Stocks finished flat as oil and yields on US government debt rose. It’s difficult to imagine anyone on earth more dedicated to Olive Garden than Braden “Breadsticks” Sinclair, a man who has embarked on an “ infinite tour of Italy ” via the Orlando-founded chain, having picked up an exclusive lifetime pasta pass seven years ago. The 33-year-old father of two has set up a website to monitor his mission since then, and has spent the equivalent of $2,100 (and around 170,000 calories) on Olive Garden pasta dishes. The only group who might give Sinclair a run for his money where reliance on the chain famed for its unlimited breadsticks is concerned? Any exec or shareholder with an active investment in Darden Restaurants . For the three-month period through August 30, 2026 (the first quarter of Darden’s fiscal 2027), Olive Garden accounted for around 42% of the restaurant group’s total revenue, even as the chain was forced to abandon a marketing campaign around its soup and salad offerings as cyclospora concerns grew. Meanwhile, LongHorn Steakhouse (again) was growing quicker than any other chain for Darden, with there being 29 more company-owned LongHorns in the world during the Darden’s fiscal first quarter compared to last year and same-store sales rising 6.2%. Olive Garden might still be the biggest brand in its parent company’s portfolio as it enters a new fiscal year, but Darden might not be able to keep relying on the Italian chain to keep investors happy. Indeed, although the OG saw same-store sales show some growth – up 1.1% – in Q1 2027, it wasn’t as much as shareholders had expected, and shares slumped on the results. However, thanks to some smoothing over on Darden’s earnings call later — the company’s CEO partly blamed the World Cup (??) for suppressed sales in the first quarter — the stock recovered some of its initial losses. Lian Yunzhi, a six-year-old speedcuber from China, recently broke the women’s world record for solving a 3x3x3 cube, clocking an average time of just 4.52 seconds across five separate solves. Within three days, Yunzhi had done it again, posting an average solve time of 4.27 seconds at a separate event certified by the World Cube Association, the official governing body of the twisty puzzle scene. While times like that might make a mere mortal of the cubing world’s mind Boggle (different grid-based activity, sorry), there are, it seems, levels to this game. Yunzhi’s parents told China Central Television that she practices two to three hours each day and has mastered over 1,300 solves or “algorithms.” It brings me no pleasure to reveal to our older readers — anyone over the age of around 10, in this specific case — that speedcubing seems to be a young person’s game in 2026, with the overall record for a single solve (2.76 seconds) set by a nine-year-old in February this year . Wendy’s just dropped a six-track, 22-minute emo/pop-punk EP called “ Songs to Listen to in a Wendy’s Parking Lot ,” with tracks including “My Frosty’s Funeral” and “It’s Not A Phase, It’s A 10PC.” It sounds exactly how you’d imagine. TamagotchAI: Mark Zuckerberg unveiled a new device called Muse Charm on Wednesday , ushering in a new palm-sized way to access Meta’s AI agent without a smartphone. Brian Niccol’s plan to make Starbucks look more like “community coffeehouses” is really taking shape… in the sense that the behemoth he helms keeps shutting them down, with another ~250 planned cafe closures across North America. Ernő Rubik, the Hungarian professor of architecture behind the eponymous puzzle, first built a prototype of the 3x3x3 cube in 1974 as a way to teach students about three-dimensional spaces. He patented the “Magic Cube” design a year later. NY Fed President John Williams due to speak on a panel at 5:15 a.m. ET. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack slated to participate in a panel discussion at 2 p.m. ET.

title: ⚠️ Higher yields and butter smuggling
body_text: If you’re packing small blocks of vacuum sealed product into your suitcase for an international flight, you’re not alone: the latest rage with American tourists is, according to the Wall Street Journal , hauling butter back from France. France is, of course, known for its fantastic butter. Much of it is what is known as cultured butter, where the cream is fermented before being churned. This process helps amp up the butterfat content of the end product and gives it that classic straw-colored hue. Cultured butter of various national origins is widely available in the US, but that hasn’t stopped the craze. The small-scale tourist import trend is, for the record, largely très bien so long as you are carrying less than five kilos into the US. “Truly melts in your mouth,” was the review in an Instagram video posted by Toronto’s Shawn Molko. While we don’t doubt the accuracy of his review, we’d suggest that artisanally-produced butter carried across international waters might be held to slightly higher standards than merely conforming to ordinary butyraceous thermal properties. Stocks dropped as oil reversed course and rose along with Treasury yields. Another day, another attempt by the US Treasury Department to lower government bond yields, and another trading session where they rose. On Wednesday, for the first time since the financial crisis, the yield on 5-year US government debt rose over 5% , a little over a week after 10-year yields crossed the same threshold. Rising global crude oil prices got yields moving higher for both US and European government debt due to inflationary fears, and better-than-expected US manufacturing and services data and a relatively weak auction added additional pressure to Treasuries, Bloomberg reported . The Treasury Department said it would buy back $6 billion in long-dated government debt as part of the previously announced plan to try to reduce supply, and thus, drive down rates. As we’ve previously covered, the bond market was underwhelmed when this program was announced earlier this month, and that mood seems little changed. Off Wall Street, the economic mood among Americans could worsen markedly: on Wednesday the rise in government bond yields pushed mortgage rates past 7% for the first time since 2024. Bloomberg reports on the struggles of Lauf, which sells high-end bikes that are assembled in the US with components made around the world and especially in China. Indeed, the heart of the global high-end carbon fiber bike industry is in Shenzen, and Lauf told Bloomberg that there is no plant in the US capable of making its lightweight frames. title: 💰 A $111B Hollywood mashup
body_text: It’s the one time of year when bulking season comes with a trophy. Fat Bear Week kicks off this week at Alaska’s Katmai National Park, where the internet gets to vote on which brown bear has done the most impressive job packing on the pounds ahead of hibernation. This year’s field is looking especially well-fed. One contender has been described as “just a balloon,” while another, Bucky, is “just a giant.” Stocks were mixed on Tuesday as oil prices continued their recent decline, falling for the fifth straight day on reports that the Saudis were close to restarting a critical pipeline that had been damaged by a Houthi attack last week. Paramount Skydance on Monday reached a settlement with a dozen states that had sued to block the firm’s acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery , paving the way for one company to own an enormous chunk of the media and entertainment market. The settlement removed the last remaining obstacle in closing the $111 billion deal , which would put Spongebob and Bugs Bunny under one roof (among many, many, many other things). Here is a recap of what the combined company would own: News: CNN and CBS, two of the largest broadcast news networks in the country, will be under one owner, along with The Free Press. The settlement calls for the formation of a “News Editorial Independence Board to establish guiding editorial and journalism principles for the combined entity’s news channels.” Television: The combined company will own more than a dozen major cable networks, including Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, MTV, Showtime and BET just to name a few. Film studios: One company will now own Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros. The settlement requires it to release a minimum of 30 theatrical films per year in the first two years of the decree, increasing to 32 films per year for the following three years. Much of the settlement, led by California, focuses on ensuring the film industry continues employing people. Streaming: HBO Max and Paramount+ now share an owner. Oh and also: David Ellison, the CEO of Paramount Skydance, is the son of Oracle co-founder and executive chairman Larry Ellison. In a deal finalized earlier this year, Oracle now owns a 15% stake in TikTok’s US operations. Combined, the father and son have influence over a solid chunk of what Americans watch on their screens big and small. After a long courthouse saga, Hollywood’s newest mega-merger is going ahead — just with a few strings attached. Paramount and Warner Bros are not the first to take advantage of a relaxed antitrust environment under the Trump administration. But few deals concentrate quite as many household-name entertainment brands in one place. Paramount-Warner would put everything from CNN and CBS to HBO, MTV, SpongeBob, Bugs Bunny, Harry Potter and Transformers inside the same corporate empire. The states that sued argued that this kind of consolidation could mean fewer movies, higher prices and fewer jobs. Rather than break up the deal, the settlement tries to put guardrails around it: Paramount has pledged to invest in film production and release a minimum amount of movies per year. More and more people are “managers” now, but only supervising AI agents. This leaves them with the snazzy title but no pay bump or opportunity to actually practice what they’re good at, Business Insider reports. That’s how much wealthier Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg got on Monday as investors celebrated the company’s new Muse AI agent, Yahoo Finance reports . GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen bought roughly $26.4 million worth of shares, according to a regulatory filing made public on Monday . Novo (previously known as Novo Nordisk ) told CNBC the company is mulling M&A opportunities. The Ozempic maker is on the hunt for its next slate of blockbuster drugs. SpaceX winding down Falcon 9, the world’s busiest rocket, is driving a rocket supply crunch, the Wall Street Journal reports . Brown bears can eat up to 90 pounds of food a day in the run-up to hibernation. General Mills earnings due out premarket.
